name: Kongai
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog kong1298: only Ivani 2024 first-mention note; no description of any kind located

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page kong1298 and reference record 679502 (hh:vw:Ivani:Kongai).
sources.note: Confirms Ivani 2024 is the sole and first descriptive reference (Glottolog's most extensive description type 'wordlist or less'); no other bibliography.

sources.citation: Ivani, Jessica K. 2024 [eScholarship cover page dates it 2023]. A field report on Kongai language from Manipur, India. Himalayan Linguistics 22(2) (Languages and Peoples of the Eastern Himalayan Region 2): 13-24. DOI 10.5070/H922259792.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent anywhere in the 12 pp. Section 2 'Syllable properties' gives syllable template (C2)C1V(Cf)[T], initials, rhymes, sesquisyllabic reduced prefixes (p.15). Footnote 6, p.16: 'This study does not deal with tone. An impressionistic account of the data, supported by comparative material, suggests that Kongai has distinctive lexical tone at the syllable level.'

sources.citation: Ivani, Jessica K. 2023b. Kongai 100-word Swadesh list (WAV audio). Zenodo.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Only primary data on the language; open audio of 100 citation forms could support a first-hand instrumental check of tone/prominence, but contains no descriptive statement.

sources.citation: Ivani, Jessica K. (future/in-prep work on Kongai and the minor Tangkhulic languages of Ukhrul district, University of Zurich) - no record found as of 2026-09-17 in CrossRef or Zenodo.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The 2024 report explicitly defers tone/prosody to future research; any follow-up by the same author would be the first source that could contain a stress or tone statement.
